tei:titleStmt.tei:title: יְיָ בּוֹקֶר אֶעֱרוֹךְ לְךָ
Hashem Boqer E'erokh Lakh (Hear my voice at dawn), a reshut by an unknown paytan (trans. Rabbi David Aaron de Sola, 1857)

tei:div.tei:head: Hashem Boqer E'erokh Lakh (Hear my voice at dawn), a reshut by an unknown paytan (trans. Rabbi David Aaron de Sola, 1857)

tei:lg.tei:l: Lord, in Thy mercy deign to hear my pray’r,
Which in the early morn I address unto Thee.
Hear my prayer, O Thou who dwellest in heaven,
When morn, even, and noon I address it unto Thee;
When my heart, as well as my eyes, is raised towards Thee;
And when, “in the greatness of Thy mercy, I enter Thine house.”
My heart panteth, my strength faileth me,
When my soul reminds me of my trespass;
Therefore do I dread to direct my steps,
“To prostrate myself in Thy holy temple.”
Oh! that I had wings like the dove,
I would fly and (perhaps) dwell secure;
But were I to ascend the heavens, there, too, is Thy dread presence.
Then “Lord guide me according to Thy righteousness.”
Oh! my soul, constantly praise thy God,
With heart and tongue intimately conjoined;
For He is the Creator and Supporter of all,
It was “he who made and established thee.” (Deuteronomy 32:6)

tei:note.tei:p: Cf. David Kimhi (1160–1235), Radak on Isaiah 58:11
